# A Metal Design Language

We develop a bioinorganic programming language in which metal coordination is used to encode structure, function, and information into nucleic acids.

## Overview

The central idea of the lab is that the hydrogen-bonding language of nucleic acids can be expanded using metal coordination chemistry.

By replacing selected hydrogen bonds with coordination bonds, we aim to create nucleic-acid systems that interact directly with electrons, light, magnetic fields, and biochemical inputs while retaining the programmability of DNA self-assembly.

## Current directions

### Metal-mediated base pairing

Designing synthetic and natural nucleobase combinations that selectively coordinate transition metals and other ions.

### Multimetallic architectures

Using DNA to position multiple metals with atomic-scale precision and create emergent electronic, magnetic, catalytic, or optical behavior.

### Inverse design

Developing computational tools that connect coordination chemistry, nucleic-acid geometry, and synthetic accessibility.
